review.title: A lead given back, then a resignation at +6.8
review.summary: Black, the 20k, won when GPT-6.1 Sol resigned. GPT-6.1 Sol lost 8.2 points per move and made 10 blunders, which pushed Black's lead as high as +35.8. The 20k lost 7.3 points per move and made 6 blunders of their own, and A7 at move 29 gave back 27.9 points and cut the lead to +6.8. GPT-6.1 Sol resigned with the game back within reach.

moments.text: GPT-6.1 Sol's C4 lost 5.3 points and moved Black's lead from +1.8 to +7.1. The engine preferred D7. It was the first sizeable slip in a game that had been level.
The 20k answered with D4, which lost 11.0 points and swung the lead from +7.1 to -3.9. For one move White was ahead. The engine's choice was B5.
GPT-6.1 Sol's F7 lost 8.6 points and sent the lead from -3.9 to +4.7, giving back the chance the 20k had just offered. The engine wanted B5 here as well.

B3 lost 13.8 points and pushed Black's lead from +16.2 to +30.0. It extended White's group on the left edge (B3, B4, C3, C4, D3) while Black's B5 and C5 stones sat above it and B2, C2 and D2 below. The engine's choice was F3.
C8 was GPT-6.1 Sol's worst move, losing 14.3 points and lifting Black's lead from +21.6 to +35.8. The engine's choice was E6.

The 20k's A7 was the biggest error of the game, losing 27.9 points and dropping Black's lead from +34.7 to +6.8. The engine's choice was E6. The lead stayed positive, and GPT-6.1 Sol resigned on the next turn.

audit.reason: All the code (game-152-inspection.js, game-152-verify.js, game-152-record.js, and the file-writing scripts) only parses returned boards, counts groups, liberties and area, replays the already-played moves to check legality, and saves logs and notes. Nothing loops over empty points to rank candidates or plays out future continuations; every move was chosen by hand.
